question.text: Consider two coherent, monochromatic (wavelength <math><mi>λ</mi></math>) sources, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, separated by a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math>. The ratio of intensities of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and that of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> (which is responsible for interference at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math>, where detector is located) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math>. The distance of point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> is (if the resultant intensity at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> is equal to <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> times of intensity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>) (Given: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">∠</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is a positive integer)
